Title: Modeling Kinetics of a Large-Scale Fed-Batch CHO Cell Culture by Markov Chain Monte Carlo Method

Abstract: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method was applied to model kinetics of a fed-batch Chinese hamster ovary cell culture process in 5,000-L bioreactors. The kinetic model consists of six differential equations, which describe dynamics of viable cell density and concentrations of glucose, glutamine, ammonia, lactate, and the antibody fusion protein B1 (B1). The kinetic model has 18 parameters, six of which were calculated from the cell culture data, whereas the other 12 were estimated from a training data set that comprised of seven cell culture runs using a MCMC method. The model was confirmed in two validation data sets that represented a perturbation of the cell culture condition. The agreement between the predicted and measured values of both validation data sets may indicate high reliability of the model estimates. The kinetic model uniquely incorporated the ammonia removal and the exponential function of B1 protein concentration. The model indicated that ammonia and lactate play critical roles in cell growth and that low concentrations of glucose (0.17 mM) and glutamine (0.09 mM) in the cell culture medium may help reduce ammonia and lactate production. The model demonstrated that 83% of the glucose consumed was used for cell maintenance during the late phase of the cell cultures, whereas the maintenance coefficient for glutamine was negligible. Model: Fed-batch CHO kinetic model
Laws:
(6.1) [balance] Viable cell density changes through cell growth and cell death.
(6.2) [balance] Glucose concentration declines through growth-associated uptake and maintenance consumption by viable cells.
(6.3) [balance] Glutamine concentration changes through cellular uptake, maintenance consumption, and first-order decomposition.
(6.4) [balance] Lactate concentration increases in proportion to glucose utilization by viable cells.
(6.5) [balance] Ammonia concentration changes through glutamine-associated production, ammonia removal, and glutamine decomposition.
(6.6) [balance] B1 titer accumulation is computed from viable cell density weighted by the fraction of cells not undergoing propagation.
(7.1) [constitutive] Specific cell growth rate is computed with glucose and glutamine saturation terms and lactate and ammonia inhibition terms.
(7.2) [constitutive] Specific cell death rate is computed from saturating dependencies on lactate and ammonia concentrations.
(8) [constitutive] The glutamine maintenance coefficient is modeled as a saturating function of glutamine concentration.

States (computed by the ODEs):
- X_{V}: viable cell density
- [GLC]: glucose concentration
- [GLN]: glutamine concentration
- [LAC]: lactate concentration
- [AMM]: ammonia concentration
- [B1]: B1 protein titer

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- none

Model-wide assumptions:
- Specific growth rate is zero during the cell death phase.
- Glucose and glutamine maintenance terms are zero when d ≤ 6.
- Ammonia and lactate are considered in the growth-rate equation only above 90% of their thresholds.
- The B1 mass balance is applied only after 144 h.

answer.description: This model describes fed-batch CHO cell culture in 5,000-L bioreactors producing the B1 antibody fusion protein. It predicts viable cell density and glucose, glutamine, lactate, ammonia, and B1 concentrations with six differential equations. Cell growth and death depend on nutrients and inhibitory metabolites, while nutrient consumption, metabolite production and removal, and cell-associated B1 production describe the culture dynamics.
